source_text: Sed per temporalem, ut dixi, dispensationem quoniam ad nostram salutem et reparationem operante dei benignitate ab illa incommutabili dei sapientia natura mutabilis nostra suscepta est, temporalium rerum salubriter pro nobis gestarum adiungimus fidem, credentes in eum dei filium, qui natus est per spiritum sanctum ex uirgine Maria. dono enim dei, hoc est sancto spiritu concessa nobis est tanta humilitas tanti dei, ut totum hominem suscipere dignaretur in utero uirginis, maternum corpus integrum inhabitans, integrum deserens. cui temporali dispensationi multis modis insidiantur haeretici. sed quisquis tenuerit catholicam fidem, ut totum hominem credat a uerbo dei esse susceptum, id est corpus, animam, spiritum, satis contra illos munitus est. quippe cum ista susceptio pro salute nostra gesta sit, cauendum est, ne, cum crediderit aliquid nostrum non pertinere ad istam susceptionem, non pertineat ad salutem. et cum homo excepta forma membrorum, quae diuersis generibus animantium diuersa tributa est, non distet a pecore nisi rationali spiritu, quae mens etiam nominatur, quomodo sana est fides, qua creditur, quod id nostrum susceperit dei sapientia, quod habemus commune cum pecore, illud autem non susceperit, quod inlustratur luce sapientiae et quod hominis proprium est?
thought_title: The earthly mission and the whole human assumed
orientation: Augustine is explaining why the creed adds faith in the Son's earthly mission, and he is defending the full assumption of body, soul, and spirit against heretics.
pass_a_gloss: But through the earthly mission, as I said, because for our salvation and repair, by the working of God's kindness, our mutable nature was taken up by that unchangeable wisdom of God, we add faith in the saving deeds of temporal things done for us, believing in him the Son of God, who was born through the Holy Spirit from the virgin Mary. For by the gift of God, that is the Holy Spirit, so great a humility of so great a God was granted to us, that he deigned to take up the whole human in the womb of the virgin, inhabiting the maternal body intact, leaving it intact. Against this earthly mission heretics plot in many ways. But whoever holds the catholic faith, so that he believes the whole human was taken up by the Word of God, that is body, soul, spirit, is sufficiently fortified against them. Since indeed this taking up was done for our salvation, one must beware lest, when he has believed something of ours does not belong to that taking up, it does not belong to salvation. And since a human, except for the shape of limbs, which has been given different to different kinds of living things, does not differ from a beast except by the rational spirit, which is also called mind, how is the faith sound, by which it is believed that the wisdom of God took up that of ours which we have in common with a beast, but did not take up that which is illuminated by the light of wisdom and which is proper to a human?

choices.why: The glossary requires this rendering for the saving plan carried out in time through Christ's incarnation, death, and resurrection.
Keeps the passive force of the Latin and the sense of the Word assuming human nature.
Preserves the totality Augustine emphasizes: body, soul, and spirit together.
Matches the cast entry for Mary and the creedal phrase.
Keeps the distinction between the rational spirit (mind) and the beastly nature, which is central to the argument.
The glossary uses 'catholic church' for ecclesia catholica; here 'catholic faith' preserves the adjective's sense of universal faith.

pass_b_english: But because of his earthly mission, as I said, our changeable nature was taken up by that unchangeable wisdom of God for our salvation and restoration, through the working of God's kindness. So we add faith in the temporal deeds beneficially done for us, believing in that Son of God who was born through the Holy Spirit from the virgin Mary. For by God's gift—that is, by the Holy Spirit—such great humility of so great a God was granted to us that he deigned to take up the whole human in the womb of the virgin, inhabiting the mother's body intact and leaving it intact. Heretics plot against this earthly mission in many ways. But whoever holds the catholic faith, believing that the whole human was taken up by the Word of God—that is, body, soul, and spirit—is well fortified against them. Since this taking up was done for our salvation, we must beware that, when one believes any part of us does not belong to that taking up, it does not belong to salvation. And since a human being, apart from the shape of the limbs which is distributed differently among different kinds of animals, does not differ from a beast except by the rational spirit, which is also called the mind, how can that faith be sound whereby one believes that God's wisdom took up what we have in common with beasts, but did not take up what is illuminated by the light of wisdom and is proper to a human being?

problems.quote: how can that faith be sound which believes
problems.source_quote: quomodo sana est fides, qua creditur
problems.why: 'Qua creditur' = 'by which it is believed' (impersonal) or 'whereby one believes'. English 'which believes' makes 'faith' the subject of 'believes', but faith doesn't believe; people believe by/through faith.
problems.fix: how can that faith be sound whereby one believes
problems.ruling: 'Qua creditur' = 'by which it is believed'; 'which believes' wrongly makes faith the subject of believing.

edits.old: how can that faith be sound which believes
edits.new: how can that faith be sound whereby one believes

fixed: Changed 'which believes' to 'whereby one believes' because the source 'qua creditur' is impersonal ('by which it is believed'), not faith as the subject of believing.

problems.why: Latin is present subjunctive in a purpose/fear clause ('cauendum est, ne... non pertineat'), not conditional 'would'. The 'ne' clause expresses fear/purpose: 'lest it not belong'.
problems.ruling: 'Cauendum est ne... non pertineat' is fear clause 'lest it not belong'; 'would not belong' misrepresents the construction.

fixed: Changed 'it would not belong' to 'lest it not belong' to render the Latin purpose/fear clause 'ne... non pertineat' correctly.

problems.quote: if someone believes any part of us did not belong to that taking up, lest it not belong to our salvation
problems.source_quote: ne, cum crediderit aliquid nostrum non pertinere ad istam susceptionem, non pertineat ad salutem
problems.why: The 'cum' is temporal ('when'), not conditional ('if'); and 'ne...non pertineat' is purpose/fear clause 'lest it not belong,' but English garbles the logic: 'when one believes X does not belong, lest Y not belong'—the 'ne' governs the whole
problems.fix: we must beware that, when one believes any part of us does not belong to that taking up, it does not belong to salvation

problems.quote: the things of time that were done for our healing
problems.source_quote: temporalium rerum salubriter pro nobis gestarum
problems.why: Latin 'rerum' means 'things/deeds' but 'salubriter' modifies 'gestarum' (done beneficially/salutarily), not 'healing' as noun; 'salutem' earlier is salvation, not healing here
problems.fix: the temporal deeds beneficially done for us
problems.ruling: 'salubriter' adverb modifies 'gestarum'; 'pro nobis' = 'for us', not 'for our healing'

problems.quote: such great humility was granted to us from so great a God
problems.why: 'tanti dei' is genitive of 'so great a God' but 'humilitas...dei' means 'humility of so great a God,' not granted 'from' God; it's God's humility, not humility coming from God to us
problems.fix: such great humility of so great a God was granted to us
problems.ruling: 'tanta humilitas tanti dei' = 'so great humility of so great a God'; God's own humility, not granted from God

edits.old: the things of time that were done for our healing
edits.new: the temporal deeds beneficially done for us

edits.old: such great humility was granted to us from so great a God
edits.new: such great humility of so great a God was granted to us

edits.old: we must beware that if someone believes any part of us did not belong to that taking up, lest it not belong to our salvation
edits.new: we must beware that, when one believes any part of us does not belong to that taking up, it does not belong to salvation

fixed: Corrected 'the things of time that were done for our healing' to 'the temporal deeds beneficially done for us' because 'salubriter' modifies 'gestarum' (done beneficially), not 'healing' as a noun.
Corrected 'such great humility was granted to us from so great a God' to 'such great humility of so great a God was granted to us' because 'tanti dei' is genitive of possession, not source.
Corrected the conditional 'if someone believes' to temporal 'when one believes' and removed the garbled 'lest' to match the source's purpose clause.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'hominem' is accusative singular masculine; 'whole human being' or 'whole man' needed, not neuter 'human'.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Human' as noun means 'human being'; normal English range for 'hominem'. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: Repeated error: 'hominem' is 'human being/man', not neuter 'human'. Occurs twice in section.
last_rejected.ruling: Same as #1; 'human' = 'human being'. Not a major error, mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: For by God's gift—that is, by the Holy Spirit—such great humility of so great a God was granted to us
last_rejected.source_quote: dono enim dei, hoc est sancto spiritu concessa nobis est tanta humilitas tanti dei
last_rejected.why: Missing 'enim' ('for'); the causal connection to preceding clause about birth from virgin is weakened.
last_rejected.fix: For by God's gift—that is, by the Holy Spirit—such great humility of so great a God was granted to us
last_rejected.ruling: English has 'For by God's gift' — 'For' renders 'enim'. Not omitted.

last_rejected.quote: how can that faith be sound whereby one believes
last_rejected.source_quote: quomodo sana est fides, qua creditur
last_rejected.why: Latin 'qua creditur' is impersonal passive 'whereby it is believed', not 'whereby one believes'; agency shifted to indefinite 'one'.
last_rejected.fix: how can that faith be sound whereby it is believed
last_rejected.ruling: 'Whereby one believes' correctly renders impersonal passive 'qua creditur'; standard equivalent.
